title: Optimize Guardrails — UI copy + gating states (draft)
content:
Context
- Optimize can propose config deltas (batching/caching/quantization/routing). Applying these changes now requires quality guardrails “gating”.
- This doc is the working draft for Console copy + visual states. Not final; expect wording changes after PM + Legal/Sec review.
- Primary surfaces:
  (1) Optimize Recommendation details → “Apply” button flow
  (2) Gating Results panel + history (post-apply and audit)
  (3) Toasts / banners for failure/timeout
  (4) Override request modal (restricted roles)

Definitions (for consistent copy)
- “Guardrails check” / “Quality checks” / “Gating eval”: we need ONE term in UI.
  Draft recommendation: use “Quality checks” in customer-facing UI; keep “Gating eval” in developer/audit details.
- “Suite”: set of evaluations run against prompt sets.
- “Prompt set”: customer + Redwood-maintained prompts used for eval.
- “Baseline”: current production config for the route/model.

Principles
- Be specific about what happened (pass/fail/timeout/partial), without over-claiming.
- Provide actionable next step in every terminal state.
- Keep blame-neutral tone. Avoid “your prompts are bad” / “your model is broken”.
- Avoid implying we “guarantee” quality. Phrase as “helps prevent regressions” / “did not detect regression in selected metrics.”
- Always link to artifacts (eval run id, prompt set revision, thresholds version) when available.

STATE MODEL (high-level)
We currently need at least 4 customer-visible states: PASS, FAIL, TIMEOUT, PARTIAL.
Additionally, there are admin/advanced states: CANCELED, ERROR, STALE, OVERRIDDEN.

State diagram (Apply flow)

  [User clicks Apply]
          |
          v
  (Pre-flight checks)
   - policy requires gating?
   - prompt set available?
   - feature flag stage (observe-only / soft-block / hard-block)
          |
          v
  [Run quality checks]
          |
          +---------------------+
          |                     |
          v                     v
       PASS                  TERMINAL NON-PASS
          |                     |
          v                     v
   [Apply config]          FAIL / TIMEOUT / PARTIAL
          |
          v
   [Post-apply monitoring note]


STATE: QUEUED / RUNNING (in-progress)
Entry conditions
- User initiated “Apply” and policy requires checks.
- Eval job created successfully and runner accepted.

UI placement
- Inline stepper in the Apply modal (preferred)
- Also show a small status chip on the recommendation card if user navigates away

Copy (modal header)
- Title: “Running quality checks”
- Subtitle (short): “We’re evaluating this change against your prompt set and Redwood benchmarks.”
- Helper text (small): “This usually takes 2–6 minutes. You can close this window; we’ll save the results.”

Progress details (optional)
- “Suite: <suite_name>”
- “Model: <model@version>”
- “Config change: <summary>”
- “Eval run ID: <id>” (copy-to-clipboard)

Buttons
- Primary: “View details” (opens side panel with metrics + run metadata)
- Secondary: “Cancel” (if we support cancellation; otherwise omit)

Error copy (if job fails to start)
- Title: “Couldn’t start quality checks”
- Body: “We ran into an internal error starting the evaluation. No changes were applied.”
- CTA: “Retry” / “Contact support”


STATE: PASS
Definition
- All required suites completed.
- Metrics meet thresholds (per policy version) with required sample sizes / CI rules.

Where shown
- Apply modal final step
- Recommendation details panel: “Quality checks: Passed”
- Audit event: stored with reasons + metric deltas

Copy (modal success)
- Title: “Quality checks passed”
- Body: “No regressions detected in the required metrics for this change.”
- Subtext: “We’ll proceed to apply the configuration update.”

Copy (post-apply confirmation)
- Title: “Change applied”
- Body: “The new configuration is now active. Monitor quality and cost in the next 24 hours.”
- Link: “View eval results” (deep link to run summary)
- Link: “View audit log”

Results panel (what to show)
- Summary line: “Passed • Policy: <policy_name>@<policy_version> • Prompt set: <name>@<rev>”
- Table columns:
  - Metric
  - Baseline
  - Proposed
  - Delta
  - Threshold
  - Status (Pass)
- Footnote: “Results are based on the prompts and metrics included in this suite.”


STATE: FAIL
Definition
- Required suites completed, and at least one required metric violates threshold.

Where shown
- Apply modal terminal state (blocked)
- Recommendation details panel: “Quality checks: Failed”

Copy (modal)
- Title: “Quality checks failed”
- Body: “This change would likely reduce output quality based on the selected evaluation suite.”
- Subtext: “No changes were applied.”

Action CTAs (modal)
- Primary: “View failed metrics”
- Secondary: “Rerun checks” (if rerun allowed)
- Tertiary (if user has permission + feature flag allows): “Request override”

Failure details panel copy
- “Failed metrics” section header
- Per-metric reason line templates:
  - “<Metric> decreased by <delta> (threshold: ≥ <threshold>).”
  - “<Metric> exceeded the maximum allowed value (threshold: ≤ <threshold>).”
  - “Minimum sample size not met for <metric> (required: <N>, observed: <n>).” (if we treat as FAIL vs PARTIAL—see open question)

Suggested next steps (small)
- “Try a smaller change (e.g., quantization profile X → Y is blocked for this model family).”
- “Add or update prompt sets to better reflect your workload.”
- “Contact support if you believe this is a false positive.”


STATE: TIMEOUT
Definition
- Runner did not return results within allowed time budget OR backlog prevented start.
- Policy outcome depends on tier + enforcement stage:
  - hard-block: block apply
  - soft-block: allow override (authorized roles)
  - observe-only: allow apply but show warning (pilot stage only)

Copy (hard-block)
- Title: “Quality checks timed out”
- Body: “We couldn’t complete the evaluation in time. To protect reliability, this change wasn’t applied.”
- Subtext: “You can retry, or request an override if this is urgent.”

Copy (soft-block)
- Title: “Quality checks timed out”
- Body: “We couldn’t complete the evaluation in time. You can retry, or apply with an override (requires approval).”
- Warning banner if proceeding with override: “Applying without completed quality checks may affect output quality.”

Copy (observe-only)
- Banner: “Quality checks timed out (observe-only). This change was applied without completed checks.”
- Note: “This mode is temporary during rollout.”

Recommended UI details for TIMEOUT
- Show “Last known status” + timestamp.
- Expose “Queue time” vs “Run time” if we have it.
- Provide a link to status page / incident banner if runner degraded.


STATE: PARTIAL
Definition (draft)
- Some suites completed but at least one required suite did not complete.
- OR metrics computed but flagged low-confidence (e.g., sample size below min).

We need to be careful: PARTIAL should not become a confusing catch-all.

Customer-facing copy options
Option A (preferred): “Incomplete” rather than “Partial”
- Title: “Quality checks incomplete”
- Body: “We couldn’t complete all required evaluations for this change.”
- Subtext: “No changes were applied.” (hard-block)

Option B: Keep “Partial results”
- Title: “Partial quality check results”
- Body: “Some evaluations completed, but results are incomplete.”

Panel content (if partial)
- “Completed checks” list
- “Incomplete checks” list with reason tags:
  - “Runner timeout”
  - “Prompt set missing”
  - “Suite error”
  - “Grader unavailable”

CTA
- Primary: “Retry incomplete checks”
- Secondary: “View completed results”
- Tertiary: “Request override” (if applicable)


STATE: OVERRIDE REQUEST (restricted)
Entry conditions
- User clicks “Request override” OR “Apply with override” (depending on product decision)
- RBAC allows requesting

Modal copy (request)
- Title: “Request override”
- Body: “Overrides allow applying this change without passing quality checks. All overrides are audited.”
- Fields:
  - “Justification” (required, min 30 chars)
    Placeholder: “Explain the urgency and why this risk is acceptable (e.g., incident mitigation, temporary test).”
  - “Duration” (optional) (e.g., 24h, 7d) if we plan time-bound overrides
  - “Notify” (optional) list: team channel/email

Buttons
- Primary: “Submit request”
- Secondary: “Cancel”

Modal copy (submitted)
- Title: “Override requested”
- Body: “Your request has been recorded and will require approval.”
- Link: “View request in audit log”

Approval copy (admin surface, if we build it)
- “Approve override”
- “Reject override”
- Warning: “Approving will apply the config change without passing required quality checks.”


STATE: APPLY BLOCKED (generic)
We will need a generic block state for policy reasons unrelated to eval results.
Examples
- “Missing required prompt set”
- “Optimization type not eligible”
- “Model version not supported for this optimization”

Copy templates
1) Missing prompt set
- Title: “Cannot run quality checks”
- Body: “This change requires a prompt set, but none is configured for this route.”
- CTA: “Configure prompt set”
- Secondary: “Learn more”

2) Model not eligible
- Title: “Change not supported for this model”
- Body: “This optimization can’t be applied to <model@version> due to known quality risks.”
- CTA: “View supported options”


CHIPS / BADGES (for list views)
- “Quality checks: Passed” (green)
- “Quality checks: Failed” (red)
- “Quality checks: Timed out” (amber)
- “Quality checks: Incomplete” (grey)
- “Override applied” (purple) — must be obvious in history


TOASTS
- Pass → apply success
  - “Quality checks passed. Applying change…”
- Fail
  - “Quality checks failed. No changes applied.”
- Timeout
  - “Quality checks timed out. Retry or request override.”


AUDIT / HISTORY COPY (read-only)
Row format (history table)
- Timestamp • Actor • Change summary • Quality checks outcome • Links

Outcome strings (must match event schema)
- PASS
- FAIL
- TIMEOUT
- INCOMPLETE
- OVERRIDDEN

Details drawer
- “Actor: <user> (role: <role>)”
- “Policy: <policy>@<version>”
- “Thresholds: <threshold_bundle>@<version>”
- “Prompt set: <name>@<rev>”
- “Eval run: <id>”
- “Override justification: <text>” (if present)


Open questions (PM / Legal / Security)
1) Term choice: “Quality checks” vs “Guardrails” vs “Gating”
   - Proposed: UI = “Quality checks”, docs can explain it’s “guardrails gating”.

2) “No regressions detected” phrasing
   - Legal concern: does this imply a warranty?
   - Alternatives:
     - “No regressions detected in the evaluated metrics.”
     - “Checks passed for the selected metrics and prompt set.”

3) PARTIAL vs INCOMPLETE naming
   - “Partial” reads like “some good news”; “Incomplete” is more direct.

4) Do we allow “Apply anyway” for any tier without formal override?
   - SRE + Sec preference: NO. Only via override with RBAC + audit.
   - Product question: do we need an emergency path for enterprise incidents?

5) Minimum sample size not met: FAIL or INCOMPLETE?
   - Applied ML suggestion (from prior discussions): treat as INCOMPLETE unless policy explicitly says “insufficient data = fail closed”.

6) Timeout behavior per tier
   - Hard-block vs “manual approval” state. Proposed:
     - Default hard-block for self-serve.
     - Enterprise: allow override request (not instant apply) with approval.

7) How visible should metric names be?
   - Concern: exposing internal rubric metric names might confuse or create support load.
   - Option: show “Task success (rubric)” with tooltip rather than raw metric id.

8) Copy for “runner degraded” incidents
   - Should we show a generic banner: “Evaluation service is currently degraded” with status page link.

9) Data privacy/PII copy (if prompt sets contain sensitive text)
   - Do we need a standard line: “Prompt text may be stored as evaluation artifacts based on your retention settings.”


Notes / next steps
- Kenji: align naming + tone with docs outline (DevEx) and PM-843 acceptance criteria.
- Naomi/Marcus: review the “no regressions detected” and override wording.
- Chloe/Felix: confirm which fields we can reliably show in UI (policy version, prompt rev, CI/confidence) without confusing users.
- Sean: confirm the timeout copy aligns with safe-degrade behavior and tier policies.

Appendix: microcopy snippets (grab bag)
- Tooltip (threshold): “The minimum acceptable value for this metric. Thresholds may vary by model family and workload.”
- Tooltip (prompt set): “A collection of prompts used to evaluate this route’s quality. You can upload your own to better match production usage.”
- Empty state (no history): “No quality checks have been run for this recommendation yet.”
- Link label: “Download eval summary (JSON)”
- Inline warning: “Results may vary with different prompts, model versions, or traffic patterns.”
